gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Xbox consoles ignore ordinary USB microphones and USB headsets. Maono's FAQ says 'The Xbox operating system deliberately does not support the generic UAC standard for audio', so a USB desk mic like the PD200XS or AM8 will not carry chat on Xbox. On Xbox the only wired chat route is a 3.5 mm headset plugged into the controller. PS5 does accept USB mics and headsets.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and got no result pages, so there is no rival page to compare against. Its own answer recommends a 'standalone USB mic' and rates it 'Great' for gaming communication without naming any platform. It never says the mic will not work at all on Xbox. Our current page shows 'Not Xbox' in a cell but gives no reason, and it does not mention the controller's 3.5 mm jack as the fix.
decides: The shopper's console decides the pick before sound quality does. On Xbox Series X|S or Xbox One, buy a 3.5 mm headset such as the EKSA E900 Pro or HyperX Cloud III and plug it into the controller. A USB desk mic (Maono PD200XS, FIFINE AM8) or USB clip-on mic (ModMic USB) gives no chat on Xbox. On PC and PS5, Sony's FAQ says most USB headsets work, and Maono and FIFINE list PS5 for their USB mics, so there the choice comes down to voice quality and desk space as ChatGPT said. A headset is the only option here that works on every console.

findings.label: Why USB mics fail on Xbox (maker's wording)
findings.value: "The Xbox operating system deliberately does not support the generic UAC standard for audio." To connect directly over USB a device "must be part of the 'Designed for Xbox' licensing program", which needs a licensing fee and an embedded authentication chip; otherwise "the Xbox sees an unauthorized device and simply ignores it." Fix given: "plug your 3.5mm headset (with its mic) directly into the controller."
findings.source_title: Why Your USB Microphone Doesn't Work on Xbox (And Why It's Not Your Fault) - Maono FAQ
findings.note: Maono's own support page (last modified 2025-11-07). UAC = USB Audio Class, the standard driver that PCs and PS5 use for USB mics.

findings.label: PS5 support for third-party USB and analog headsets
findings.value: "most USB and analog headsets will be supported"; headsets on a 3.5mm jack, USB-A or USB-C "will work for 3D Audio"; third-party Bluetooth headsets "will not be supported on PS5"
findings.note: Sony's own launch FAQ from 2020, still online. It shows PS5 does not have the Xbox USB-audio block.

findings.label: What a 3.5 mm headset loses on Xbox (maker example)
findings.value: Arctis Nova 3 "can be used with Xbox by connecting it through the controller's 3.5mm headset jack"; in that mode "USB-based features are not available" (RGB, Sonar); it works as a basic analog headset
findings.source_title: Can the Arctis Nova 3 support Xbox - SteelSeries Support
findings.note: A second maker reaching the same conclusion: on Xbox, USB audio features drop out and only the analog 3.5 mm path works. By the same logic, USB-only extras such as the E900 Pro's 7.1 USB mode should be lost on Xbox.
